title: 2026–27 Flu, COVID-19 and RSV Vaccine Recommendations - Johns Hopkins Medicine

analysis.event: Johns Hopkins Medicine provides updated vaccine recommendations for flu, COVID-19, and RSV for the 2026–27 season.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Vaccination is recommended for most people age 6 months and older to reduce the risk of infection and severe illness.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Vaccination is advised as a preventive measure, and treatments are available for those who get infected.

analysis.brief_en: Johns Hopkins Medicine has released updated vaccine recommendations for the 2026–27 flu, COVID-19, and RSV seasons. The article emphasizes the importance of vaccination for most individuals aged 6 months and older to safeguard against seasonal illnesses. It outlines that flu season typically starts near the end of October and peaks between December and February, with the vaccine taking about two weeks to provide protection. The CDC recommends annual flu vaccines for people aged 6 months and older, with specific dosing requirements for children under 9 years old. A new mRNA flu vaccine (mFLUSIVA) is available for adults 50 and older. For COVID-19, the article states that vaccines are updated annually to target the most relevant strains and are recommended for all individuals 6 months and older. It highlights that vaccination is especially important for high-risk groups such as adults 65 and older, immunocompromised individuals, long-term-care residents, and pregnant women. The article also mentions that antiviral medications can be used for those who test positive for COVID-19 and are at increased risk for severe illness. Additionally, it notes that the RSV vaccine and antibody treatments are available for certain high-risk children and infants.
